questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in Austria last summer, in the small town my grandmother is origianlly from. I had a really god time and decided that doing a full semester in Austria would be nice. I chose Austria over Germany because of personal connections but part of the reason to go abroad was to improve my language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite esay. The Wien Uni webside has all informations and also they are very helpful at the international office if you have questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was orientation and it was easy to ask for help is needed. They send out emails with all informations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with family, so easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start in advance and look for a nice WG - that's probably the nicest way to live in Vienna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with family, I have no idea about student housing - I only know what I heard from friends. They would always recomment WG over a doorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very different from home, but easy to get help!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I took my electives in Vienna and therefor had courses on different institutes meaning that there were different ways to do it. First of all the registration period is different from institutet ot institute, then through u:find you find the wanted course and apply. There is no first come first serve. In some cases this was all, in others you had to wait and then show up to the first class to make sure that your spot was secured and lastly for some I had to devide out points depending on how much I wanted the spot. For me it was not a problem, but I can be hard to get a spot and therefor many apply for more courses than they are going to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked to many proffessors that helped me seleced courses and also to my ESN boddy that explained the system.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ast proffesors for help choosing courses that fits for you! And start early - it's a quite time consuming procces.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to take many small courses, it's a mess, the level is low.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Many of the courses I took was 1./2. semester courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had 3 courses that were lectures quite similars to the one I'm use to from UCPH. Then I also had 2 seminar courses. These don't have exams but things you have to hand in during the semester. Also there are more descussion in these and the group is smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
480045-1 VO Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian Regional and Cultural
480012-1 VO East Slavic Regional and Cultural Studies
220033-1 UE GESKO B: UE JOUR Journalism
220051-1 UE METH: UE QUALI Qualitative Research Methods
070312-1 VO Political System of Austria and the EU

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the taskes we had to do in 220033-1 UE GESKO B: UE JOUR Journalism - it was very practical and we had good discussions about our work. Also 480045-1 VO Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian Regional and Cultural was very nice! I liked the professor a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went home to Denmark a couple of times, that costed extra...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things a similar to DK in terms of pricing. Alcohol and going out is a bit cheaper, shopping is kind of the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Look for ESN events in the begining - they organize a lot!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Theres always a lot going on in Vienna. Some at the university but besides uni sprot and ESN i didn't use the university offers much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are always many options in and around Vienna - go to one of the museums, outdoor raves, bouldering gyms, wine hikes, old cafés, hang out in the parks, at Donauinsel, fleamarkets - 1000things is a good SoMe account to follow.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as above - and take advantage of the fact that you are in Austia! Go hiking, climbing, swimming or whatever fits you.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It's similar to DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No. I hung out with international students mostly. Maybe speak german? Try Bumble Friends? Idk. Uni is not very social and it was not a priority of mine to make local friends rather than other friends. A WG might also be a good place to make local friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: To me it's not very different but I did appreciate how proud of their culture they were. Also stupid sometimes, but mostly nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Vienna is an amazing city! Use it and all it has to offer!

2. Go for seminar classes - then you don't have as many exams in the end (also because the courses are small in terms of ects) and it is more social and have more discussions.

3. The professors are happy to help! Ask questions, for help with projects and so on.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it's important to be aware of what type of courses you take. Don't go for too many lectures with multiple choise exams in the end... NOT fun.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really really had a good time, especially the last two month where I found my base and friend group. I think everyone should go. Even though it's also hard sometimes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The homesickness that comes and goes. It's hard to be far away from home when something is going on, that you would like to be part of. Not all days are good. They also aren't at home, that's maybe worth remembering... But then just rely on your new friends! They feel the same way sometimes - eveyone do!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
